Hi Mel, quick general rundown — I haven't seen your leg, so take this as forum-level advice rather than a diagnosis.

What you're describing — morning stiffness, soreness 3-4cm up from the heel, a bit of a lump, easing with running then aching that night, plus the jump from 30 to 48k in three weeks — reads like a classic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy. That's a load problem rather than a tear, but no-one can diagnose it properly over the internet.

Heel drops are fine, but these days the better evidence is for heavy slow calf raises: three sets of 15, twice a day, slow up and slow down (about three seconds each way), starting both legs and building to single leg off a step. On the bad days, switch to isometric holds — five reps of 30-45 seconds at mid-range — which can settle it without loading through range.

Two things to skip. Hard stretching into the tendon, "till it burns", tends to irritate it more than help. And cortisone injections near the tendon are worth avoiding: short-term relief, but worse outcomes longer term and a real risk of rupture, especially if you keep running on it.

For pain, a rough guide is up to 3/10 while you're loading is acceptable as long as it's settled by the next morning and back to baseline. If it's stiffer or sorer the day after, that was too much — drop the volume back. You don't need to stop completely; cut the k's, keep it flat, and park the speedwork for a few weeks.

Red flags: sudden pop, a feeling like a kick in the back of the leg, or you can't push off or do a single-leg heel raise — stop running and the calf work and get it checked that day, GP or ED, because that's how a rupture presents.

One more general thing worth knowing: some antibiotics, the fluoroquinolone ones, are linked to tendon problems, so mention any recent antibiotics to whoever assesses you.

If it's not settling in 3-4 weeks, see a sports physio. Plenty around Bayswater — doesn't have to be me.
